summary.text: Kathy Castor is the Democratic incumbent in Florida's 14th Congressional District, first elected in 2006. An attorney who began her career at the Florida Department of Community Affairs, she served on the Hillsborough County Commission before Congress. She is running on her record in the House, according to her campaign website.

paragraphs.text: Born in Miami, Florida, in 1966; her congressional biography says she graduated from Tampa's Chamberlain High School, Emory University and Florida State University College of Law.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Emory University (1988) and a J.D. from Florida State University College of Law (1991).

According to her congressional biography, she started her legal career with the Florida Department of Community Affairs, enforcing environmental and growth management laws, and later practiced as a land use and environmental attorney representing local governments.
Her congressional biography also lists her as a former president of the Florida Association of Women Lawyers and a partner in a statewide law firm.
Served on the Hillsborough County Board of Commissioners from 2002 to 2006, including as chair of the Hillsborough County Environmental Protection Commission.
First elected to the U.S. House in 2006; she is the first woman to represent both Hillsborough and Pinellas Counties in Congress, according to her office.
Served on the Rules Committee in her first term and chaired the House Select Committee on the Climate Crisis from 2019 to 2022.

Currently serves on the Energy and Commerce Committee, where she is Ranking Member of the Energy Subcommittee, and on the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party.

Her biography states she and her husband have two daughters and that she is the daughter of former Hillsborough County Judge Don Castor and former University of South Florida president and Education Commissioner Betty Castor.
